### Before

The full authorization URL was hidden on the success path. Enter opened the default browser, and only then did callback waiting begin:

```text
entire login
Logging in to: https://us.auth.entire.io

Press Enter to open in browser...
Waiting for sign-in... ✓ Login complete.
```

There was no built-in copy action. The complete URL appeared only as a fallback after browser launch failed.

### After

The complete authorization URL is always displayed on its own indented line. Waiting starts immediately. In this example the user presses `c`, then Enter, so both actions are acknowledged before login completes:

```text
entire login

Waiting for sign-in…
✓ Copied to clipboard.
✓ Opened browser.
✓ Login complete.
```

```text
[Enter] Open browser  [c] Copy URL
Waiting for approval…
✓ Copied to clipboard.
✓ Opened browser.
✓ Login complete.
```

Description:
Problem:
The login flow's "Press Enter to open in browser" prompt was unclear and unreliable. Users had no visibility into whether a browser would actually open, and the fallback URL only appeared if the browser open failed. In non-interactive or headless environments (CI, SSH sessions), the behavior was confusing.
Solution:
Replaced the implicit "press Enter" interaction with an explicit three-option prompt: [Enter] Continue  [c] Copy URL  [o] Open in default browser. The full login URL is now always visible, and users can:
Press Enter to continue without opening anything (non-blocking in headless/non-TTY environments)
Press c to copy the URL to clipboard and stay at the prompt
Press o to open the default browser
The implementation uses raw terminal mode with escape-sequence-aware event parsing (via charmbracelet/ultraviolet) so that arrow keys and function-key sequences don't trigger unintended actions. Terminal state is restored before returning. In test or non-TTY contexts, pressing Enter silently continues without side effects. The loginURLInteractor struct makes the three side effects (read action, copy, open) injectable for parallel tests.

148	// parseLoginServer validates and canonicalises the --server value: an
149	// http(s) origin with nothing but scheme and host. Userinfo, path, query,
150	// and fragment are rejected rather than silently dropped — the value
151	// becomes the OAuth issuer, the token-exchange target, and the keyring
152	// key, so surprising rewrites would surface as confusing auth failures
153	// much later. A lone trailing slash is tolerated (normalised away).
154	func parseLoginServer(raw string) (string, error) {
155		raw = strings.TrimSpace(raw)
156		if raw == "" {
157			return "", errors.New("empty server URL")
158		}
159		u, err := url.Parse(raw)
160		if err != nil {
161			return "", fmt.Errorf("parse server URL: %w", err)
162		}
163		// Error messages echo u.Redacted(), not raw: the URL may carry
164		// userinfo (that's one of the rejection cases), and stderr often ends
165		// up in CI logs where a password must not appear.
166		switch {
167		case u.Scheme != schemeHTTPS && u.Scheme != schemeHTTP:
168			return "", fmt.Errorf("scheme must be http or https, got %q", u.Redacted())
169		case u.Host == "":
170			return "", fmt.Errorf("missing host in %q", u.Redacted())
171		case u.User != nil:
172			return "", fmt.Errorf("userinfo not allowed in %q", u.Redacted())
173		case u.Path != "" && u.Path != "/":
174			return "", fmt.Errorf("path not allowed in %q (use the bare origin)", u.Redacted())
175		case u.RawQuery != "" || u.Fragment != "":
176			return "", fmt.Errorf("query/fragment not allowed in %q", u.Redacted())
177		}
178		return api.NormalizeOriginURL(raw), nil
179	}

245	// runLoginAuto picks between the browser (loopback authorization-code) and
246	// device-code flows and runs the chosen one. The browser flow is the
247	// default — no code to type, no poll latency — but it needs a browser that
248	// can reach this machine's 127.0.0.1, so headless terminals (CI, piped
249	// stdin), SSH sessions, and a loopback listener that fails to start all
250	// fall back to the device flow with a one-line explanation; the same
251	// both-flows-with-fallback shape gh / gcloud / aws sso ship. --device
252	// forces the device flow without commentary.
253	func runLoginAuto(ctx context.Context, outW, errW io.Writer, deviceClient deviceAuthClient, startBrowser func(context.Context) (browserAuthFlow, error), urlInteractor loginURLInteractor, facts loginFlowFacts) error {
254		if shouldUseBrowserLogin(facts) {
255			flow, err := startBrowser(ctx)
256			if err != nil {
257				// Binding the loopback listener can fail (sandboxing, firewall,
258				// exhausted ports); that shouldn't strand the user — warn and
259				// use the device flow instead.
260				fmt.Fprintf(errW, "Warning: could not start browser sign-in (%v); falling back to the device-code flow.\n", err)
261				return runLogin(ctx, outW, errW, deviceClient, urlInteractor, facts.canPrompt)
262			}
263			return runBrowserLogin(ctx, outW, errW, flow, deviceClient.BaseURL(), urlInteractor, browserLoginTimeout)
264		}
265		switch {
266		case facts.useDevice:
267			// Explicitly requested; no explanation needed.
268		case !facts.canPrompt:
269			fmt.Fprintln(errW, "No interactive terminal detected; using device-code flow.")
270		case facts.sshSession:
271			fmt.Fprintln(errW, "SSH session detected; using device-code flow (a browser opened here couldn't reach this machine).")
272		}
273		return runLogin(ctx, outW, errW, deviceClient, urlInteractor, facts.canPrompt)
274	}

296	// runBrowserLogin runs the loopback authorization-code flow on an
297	// already-started flow: show the authorization URL and explicit actions, wait
298	// up to waitTimeout for the redirect back to the local listener, then exchange
299	// the code for tokens. Shares the token validation + persistence tail with
300	// runLogin via persistLogin.
301	func runBrowserLogin(ctx context.Context, outW, errW io.Writer, flow browserAuthFlow, baseURL string, urlInteractor loginURLInteractor, waitTimeout time.Duration) error {
302		// Wait tears the listener down on return, but Close is idempotent and
303		// covers the error paths before Wait runs.
304		defer func() { _ = flow.Close() }()
305	
306		authURL := flow.AuthorizationURL()
307		fmt.Fprintf(outW, "Logging in to %s\n\n", baseURL)
308		printLoginURL(outW, browserLoginURLLabel, authURL)
309	
310		// Start the deadline as soon as the URL is visible. Waiting for the
311		// loopback redirect and reading URL actions then proceed concurrently, so
312		// clicking or pasting the URL can complete login without a terminal key.
313		waitCtx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(ctx, waitTimeout)
314		defer cancel()
315	
316		code, err := waitForLoginURLResult(
317			waitCtx,
318			outW,
319			errW,
320			authURL,
321			"Waiting for sign-in… ",
322			urlInteractor,
323			flow.Wait,
324		)
325		if err != nil {
326			if errors.Is(waitCtx.Err(), context.DeadlineExceeded) {
327				return fmt.Errorf("timed out waiting for sign-in after %v; run `entire login` again, or use `entire login --device`", waitTimeout)
328			}
329			return fmt.Errorf("complete login: %w", err)
330		}
331	
332		token, refreshToken, err := flow.Exchange(ctx, code)
333		if err != nil {
334			return fmt.Errorf("complete login: %w", err)
335		}
336	
337		return persistLogin(outW, baseURL, token, refreshToken)
338	}

341	// the shared contexts.json credential model. Shared by the device-code and
342	// browser flows.
343	func persistLogin(outW io.Writer, baseURL, token, refreshToken string) error {
344		if err := validateReceivedToken(token, baseURL, time.Now()); err != nil {
345			return fmt.Errorf("reject login token: %w", err)
346		}
347	
348		// Record the login in the shared contexts.json credential model — the
349		// single store every consumer (control plane, data API, git remote
350		// helper, entiredb's CLIs) resolves against.
351		if _, err := auth.RecordLoginContext(token, refreshToken, true); err != nil {
352			return fmt.Errorf("save login: %w", withHeadlessStoreHint(err))
353		}

359	// withHeadlessStoreHint appends file-token-store guidance to a credential
360	// store write failure. The default backend is the OS keyring, which locked
361	// or keyring-less machines (CI, containers, minimal server VMs) can't use —
362	// the raw store error gives those users no way forward (#1036). The hint is
363	// skipped when ENTIRE_TOKEN_STORE=file is already set (suggesting it again
364	// would be nonsense) and for failures the file store wouldn't help with.
365	func withHeadlessStoreHint(err error) error {
366		if !errors.Is(err, auth.ErrCredentialStoreWrite) || tokenstore.FileBackendSelected() {
367			return err
368		}
369	
370		return fmt.Errorf("%w\n\nIf this machine has no usable OS keyring (headless server, container, CI), store tokens in a file instead:\n\n  %s=file entire login\n\nTokens are then written with 0600 permissions to %s (override the location with %s)",
371			err, tokenstore.BackendEnvVar, tokenstore.FileBackendPath(), tokenstore.PathEnvVar)

374	// validateReceivedToken runs minimum-trust checks on the access token
375	// the AS handed us before we persist it. The server is the authority
376	// on signature/exp; this is defense in depth aimed at catching gross
377	// misbehaviour by a compromised or misconfigured AS (e.g. handing back
378	// a token from a different issuer than the one we asked, or one whose
379	// claims are already-expired).
380	//
381	// It also enforces what the contexts model needs up front:
382	// RecordLoginContext — the sole persistence path — keys the context and
383	// keychain slot on the token's iss and handle/sub claims, so a token
384	// without parseable claims can never complete a login. Rejecting it here
385	// names the requirement instead of surfacing a parse error from the save
386	// step. Entire-core always issues claim-bearing JWTs; opaque-token-only
387	// servers are not supported.
388	func validateReceivedToken(rawToken, issuerURL string, now time.Time) error {
389		claims, err := tokens.ParseClaims(rawToken)
390		if errors.Is(err, tokens.ErrUnsignedJWT) {
391			return err //nolint:wrapcheck // sentinel surfaces verbatim for caller's errors.Is
392		}
393		if err != nil {
394			return fmt.Errorf("login server issued a token without parseable JWT claims (claim-bearing JWTs are required): %w", err)
395		}
396		if claims.Issuer == "" {
397			return errors.New("token has no iss claim; cannot record a login context")
398		}
399		if claims.Handle == "" && claims.Subject == "" {
400			return errors.New("token has no handle or sub claim; cannot record a login context")
401		}
402	
403		// iss check: the token must claim to come from the issuer we sent
404		// the device-code request to. A mismatch means either the AS is
405		// misconfigured or someone's playing games.
406		if issErr := issMatches(claims.Issuer, issuerURL); issErr != nil {
407			return issErr
408		}
409	
410		// exp sanity: a token that's already expired before we even store
411		// it is a smell. Don't reject if exp is unset (some servers omit).
412		if !claims.ExpiresAt.IsZero() && !now.Before(claims.ExpiresAt) {
413			return fmt.Errorf("token already expired (exp=%s, now=%s)",
414				claims.ExpiresAt.Format(time.RFC3339), now.Format(time.RFC3339))
415		}
416	
417		return nil
418	}
419	
420	// issMatches reports whether claimed equals expected after stripping path/
421	// query/fragment via api.OriginOnly, so "https://issuer/" and "https://issuer"
422	// match. The caller has already rejected an empty iss claim.
423	func issMatches(claimed, expected string) error {
424		normClaimed := api.OriginOnly(claimed)
425		normExpected := api.OriginOnly(expected)
426		if normClaimed != normExpected {
427			return fmt.Errorf("iss mismatch: token claims %q, expected %q", normClaimed, normExpected)
428		}
429		return nil
430	}

432	func waitForApproval(ctx context.Context, poller deviceAuthClient, deviceCode string, expiresIn int, interval, slowDownBackoff time.Duration) (accessToken, refreshToken string, err error) {
433		expiry := time.Duration(expiresIn) * time.Second
434		if expiry <= 0 || expiry > maxExpiresIn {
435			expiry = maxExpiresIn
436		}
437		deadline := time.Now().Add(expiry)
438		pollInterval := interval
439		if pollInterval <= 0 {
440			pollInterval = fallbackDeviceAuthPollInterval
441		}
442	
443		consecutiveErrors := 0
444	
445		for {
446			if time.Now().After(deadline) {
447				return "", "", errors.New("device authorization expired")
448			}
449	
450			result, err := poller.PollDeviceAuth(ctx, deviceCode)
451			if err != nil {
452				consecutiveErrors++
453				if consecutiveErrors >= maxTransientErrors {
454					return "", "", fmt.Errorf("poll approval status (after %d consecutive failures): %w", consecutiveErrors, err)
455				}
456				// Transient error — wait and retry.
457				select {
458				case <-ctx.Done():
459					return "", "", fmt.Errorf("wait for approval: %w", ctx.Err())
460				case <-time.After(pollInterval):
461				}
462				continue
463			}
464			consecutiveErrors = 0
465	
466			switch result.Error {
467			case "":
468				if result.AccessToken == "" {
469					return "", "", errors.New("device authorization completed without a token")
470				}
471				return result.AccessToken, result.RefreshToken, nil
472			case "authorization_pending":
473				// no-op, will sleep and retry below
474			case "slow_down":
475				pollInterval += slowDownBackoff
476				if pollInterval > maxPollInterval {
477					pollInterval = maxPollInterval
478				}
479			case "access_denied":
480				return "", "", errors.New("device authorization denied")
481			case "expired_token":
482				return "", "", errors.New("device authorization expired")
483			default:
484				if result.ErrorDescription != "" {
485					return "", "", fmt.Errorf("device authorization failed: %s: %s", result.Error, result.ErrorDescription)
486				}
487				return "", "", fmt.Errorf("device authorization failed: %s", result.Error)
488			}
489	
490			select {
491			case <-ctx.Done():
492				return "", "", fmt.Errorf("wait for approval: %w", ctx.Err())
493			case <-time.After(pollInterval):
494			}
495		}
496	}

535	// waitForLoginURLResult runs authentication and terminal input concurrently.
536	// A completed authentication cancels and joins the input reader before
537	// returning, which guarantees Bubble Tea restores the terminal from raw mode.
538	// Copy leaves both actions available; a successful browser open stops reading
539	// keys and waits only for authentication to finish.
540	func waitForLoginURLResult[T any](
541		ctx context.Context,
542		outW, errW io.Writer,
543		loginURL, waitingMessage string,
544		interactor loginURLInteractor,
545		wait func(context.Context) (T, error),
546	) (T, error) {
547		flowCtx, cancelFlow := context.WithCancel(ctx)
548		defer cancelFlow()
549	
550		actionCtx, cancelAction := context.WithCancel(flowCtx)
551		defer cancelAction()
552	
553		waitCh := make(chan loginURLWaitResult[T], 1)
554		go func() {
555			value, err := wait(flowCtx)
556			waitCh <- loginURLWaitResult[T]{value: value, err: err}
557		}()
558	
559		actionCh := make(chan loginURLActionResult, 1)
560		actionActive := false
561		startActionRead := func() {
562			actionActive = true
563			go func() {
564				action, err := interactor.readAction(actionCtx)
565				actionCh <- loginURLActionResult{action: action, err: err}
566			}()
567		}
568		finishActionRead := func() {
569			cancelAction()
570			if actionActive {
571				<-actionCh
572				actionActive = false
573			}
574		}
575	
576		statusLineOpen := false
577		renderInitialPrompt := func() {
578			fmt.Fprintln(outW, loginURLPrompt)
579			fmt.Fprint(outW, waitingMessage)
580			statusLineOpen = true
581		}
582		finishStatusLine := func() {
583			if statusLineOpen {
584				fmt.Fprintln(outW)
585				statusLineOpen = false
586			}
587		}
588		renderInitialPrompt()
589		startActionRead()
590	
591		for {
592			select {
593			case result := <-waitCh:
594				finishActionRead()
595				finishStatusLine()
596				return result.value, result.err
597			case result := <-actionCh:
598				actionActive = false
599				finishStatusLine()
600	
601				// Authentication may have completed at the same time as the key
602				// arrived. Prefer that result over launching a stale side effect.
603				select {
604				case waitResult := <-waitCh:
605					cancelAction()
606					return waitResult.value, waitResult.err
607				default:
608				}
609	
610				if result.err != nil {
611					cancelFlow()
612					<-waitCh
613					var zero T
614					return zero, result.err
615				}
616	
617				switch result.action {
618				case loginURLNone:
619					// A controlling TTY disappeared between prompt detection and
620					// use (or tests disabled real terminal input). Authentication
621					// still runs and can complete through the visible URL.
622					cancelAction()
623					result := <-waitCh
624					return result.value, result.err
625				case loginURLCopy:
626					if err := interactor.copyURL(loginURL); err != nil {
627						fmt.Fprintf(errW, "Warning: failed to copy login URL: %v\n", err)
628					} else {
629						fmt.Fprintln(outW, "✓ Copied to clipboard.")
630					}
631					startActionRead()
632				case loginURLOpen:
633					if err := interactor.openURL(flowCtx, loginURL); err != nil {
634						fmt.Fprintf(errW, "Warning: failed to open default browser: %v\n", err)
635						startActionRead()
636						continue
637					}
638	
639					cancelAction()
640					fmt.Fprintln(outW, "✓ Opened browser.")
641					result := <-waitCh
642					finishStatusLine()
643					return result.value, result.err
644				default:
645					cancelFlow()
646					<-waitCh
647					var zero T
648					return zero, fmt.Errorf("unexpected login URL action: %d", result.action)
649				}
650			}
651		}
652	}

654	// readLoginURLAction reads a single key from the controlling terminal without
655	// consuming piped stdin. Missing TTYs disable key actions while authentication
656	// continues through the always-visible URL.
657	func readLoginURLAction(ctx context.Context) (loginURLAction, error) {
658		// In-process and forced-interactive subprocess tests must never touch a
659		// developer's real terminal. Authentication itself continues concurrently.
660		if interactive.UnderTest() {
661			return loginURLNone, nil
662		}
663	
664		tty, err := os.OpenFile("/dev/tty", os.O_RDWR, 0)
665		if err != nil {
666			return loginURLNone, nil //nolint:nilerr // no controlling TTY; continue without key actions
667		}

669		return readLoginURLActionFromTTY(ctx, tty)

672	// readLoginURLActionFromTTY takes ownership of tty. Bubble Tea handles raw mode,
673	// escape-sequence decoding, cancellation, and terminal restoration. If the
674	// terminal cannot provide single-key input, disable key actions.
675	func readLoginURLActionFromTTY(ctx context.Context, tty *os.File) (loginURLAction, error) {
676		defer tty.Close()
677		if !interactive.IsTerminalReader(tty) {
678			return loginURLNone, nil
679		}
680	
681		model := loginURLActionModel{}
682		finalModel, err := tea.NewProgram(
683			model,
684			tea.WithContext(ctx),
685			tea.WithInput(tty),
686			tea.WithOutput(io.Discard),
687			tea.WithoutSignalHandler(),
688		).Run()
689		if ctx.Err() != nil {
690			return loginURLNone, fmt.Errorf("interrupted: %w", ctx.Err())

701		// instead of SIGINT. Record the equivalent process signal before returning
702		// context.Canceled so main preserves the CLI's normal quiet SIGINT/130 exit
703		// semantics (including breaking an enclosing shell loop).

733		}
734	
735		m.selected = true

737	}

Reviewed the branch, PR #1961, and Trail #1020.

## CI status

**The lint failure is not real.** The job died downloading the golangci-lint v2.11.3 binary (`socket hang up`, two retries, then `##[error]Failed to run`) — golangci-lint never executed. I ran `mise run lint` locally on this tree: **0 issues**, gofmt/gomod/shellcheck clean. Everything else passes (test-core, 3 integration shards, both canaries, windows). "Entire Gates" is failing only because it aggregates lint. Just re-run the job.

Login tests also pass under `-race -count=2`.

## The design holds up

The concurrency shape in `waitForLoginURLResult` is correct as far as I can trace it: both channels are buffered 1, only one reader goroutine is ever live (`startActionRead` is only re-armed after the previous result is drained), every terminal path cancels *and* joins the reader, and the `select`/`default` at login.go:603 correctly prefers a completed auth over acting on a stale keypress.

The `procsignal.Store(os.Interrupt)` fix (87061eae1) is the right call — raw mode does turn Ctrl-C into a keypress, and I confirmed against `cmd/entire/main.go` that this is what `dieFromSignal`/`terminatingSignal` consume. Worth noting the inverse race is safe too: the success path never consults `procsignal`, so Ctrl-C landing exactly as login completes can't turn a successful login into exit 130.

Also fine: `atotto/clipboard` was already in the module graph indirectly (via the charm deps), so promoting it to direct adds no new dependency surface. OSC 8 degrades properly — literal URL always printed, `ShouldStyle` gates the wrap, non-http schemes skip it. Every claim in the PR body checks out against the code (5-minute deadline starting at URL display, device expiry capped at 15m, headless/SSH keeping the prompt-free path).

## Findings

**1. The one behavior this feature lives or dies on is untested.** `waitForLoginURLResult`'s doc comment makes the load-bearing claim: *"A completed authentication cancels and joins the input reader before returning, which guarantees Bubble Tea restores the terminal from raw mode."* But `TestWaitForLoginURLResult_CompletesWithoutActionAndJoinsReader` proves that with a fake `readAction` that returns on `ctx.Done()` — it tests the harness, not Bubble Tea. The real-PTY tests in `login_tty_test.go` only drive `readLoginURLActionFromTTY` directly with a keypress, Ctrl-C, or a non-TTY. Nothing verifies a real `tea.Program` on a real PTY actually returns when `actionCtx` is canceled.

If it doesn't, `finishActionRead()`'s `<-actionCh` (login.go:571) blocks forever *after a successful sign-in*, with the terminal still in raw mode. That's the worst failure this change can produce, and the suite would be green. Cheap to close — you already have the primitives:

```go
ptmx, tty, observer, before := openLoginPromptPTY(t)
interactor.readAction = func(ctx context.Context) (loginURLAction, error) {
    return readLoginURLActionFromTTY(ctx, tty)
}
// wait() returns immediately; assert waitForLoginURLResult returns within a
// deadline, then assertLoginPromptTTYRestored(t, observer, before).
```

**2. `readLoginURLActionFromTTY` swallows every Bubble Tea error** (login.go:693, `if err != nil { return loginURLNone, nil }`). That's the fallback Copilot asked for, but it's now blanket: any startup failure silently disables key actions while the prompt still advertises them. A one-line stderr warning would make it diagnosable.

**3. The prompt is printed before we know keys are readable.** `renderInitialPrompt()` runs ahead of `startActionRead()`, so on any `loginURLNone` return the user has been told about two keys that do nothing. `canPrompt` gates the common cases so this is mostly test-mode, but it's a promise the code can't keep.

**4. Dead call at login.go:642.** `finishStatusLine()` in the `loginURLOpen` success path can never fire — line 599 already ran it at the top of the `actionCh` case, so `statusLineOpen` is always false by then.

**5. `clipboard.WriteAll` runs on the select loop's goroutine** (login.go:626) and takes no context. On Linux it shells out to xclip/xsel; a hung helper stalls processing of the auth result. Low likelihood, but copy is the one action that doesn't need to be synchronous.

## Stale records

**The PR reply on `login.go:679` points at a test that no longer exists.** It says the `term.MakeRaw` fallback is verified by `TestReadLoginURLActionFromTTY_RawModeFailureContinuesAndCloses` — the Bubble Tea refactor (c44e3cdac) removed the direct `term.MakeRaw` call and replaced that test with `TestReadLoginURLActionFromTTY_UnavailableInputContinuesAndCloses`, which covers the non-TTY path, not raw-mode failure. Behavior is still fine; the audit trail on the PR now resolves to nothing.

**Trail #1020's description documents the superseded design.** It describes a three-option prompt (`[Enter] Continue  [c] Copy URL  [o] Open in default browser`), says Enter continues *without opening anything*, and credits `charmbracelet/ultraviolet`. What shipped is `[Enter] Open browser  [c] Copy URL`, waiting starts immediately, and it's built on `charm.land/bubbletea/v2`. Trail is phase `building` with no findings and no approvals. Since the trail is the durable context record for this branch, it's worth an `entire trail update` before this lands — the PR body is accurate and would make a good replacement.

+// test from passing because authentication won a startup race before Bubble Tea

+func TestWaitForLoginURLResult_AuthCompletionCancelsTTYAndRestoresTerminal(t *testing.T) {
+	t.Parallel()
+
+	ptmx, tty, observer, before := openLoginPromptPTY(t)
+	defer ptmx.Close()
+	defer observer.Close()
+
+	authComplete := make(chan struct{})
+	interactor := loginURLInteractor{
+		readAction: func(ctx context.Context) (loginURLAction, error) {
+			return readLoginURLActionFromTTY(ctx, tty)
+		},
+		copyURL: noopCopyURL,
+		openURL: noopOpenURL,
+	}
+
+	resultCh := make(chan loginURLWaitResult[string], 1)
+	go func() {
+		value, err := waitForLoginURLResult(
+			context.Background(),
+			io.Discard,
+			io.Discard,
+			"https://auth.test/authorize",
+			"Waiting... ",
+			interactor,
+			func(context.Context) (string, error) {

+			},
+		)
+		resultCh <- loginURLWaitResult[string]{value: value, err: err}
+	}()
+
+	waitForLoginPromptTTYRaw(t, observer, before)
+	close(authComplete)
+
+	select {
+	case result := <-resultCh:

**1. The one behavior this feature lives or dies on is untested.** `waitForLoginURLResult`'s doc comment makes the load-bearing claim: *"A completed authentication cancels and joins the input reader before returning, which guarantees Bubble Tea restores the terminal from raw mode."* But `TestWaitForLoginURLResult_CompletesWithoutActionAndJoinsReader` proves that with a fake `readAction` that returns on `ctx.Done()` — it tests the harness, not Bubble Tea.
